cleansingStrength.rationale: Low: genuinely mild architecture - mild amino-acid-type anionic Sodium Methyl Cocoyl Taurate #2 buffered by Decyl Glucoside #3, Cocamidopropyl Betaine #4 and Coco-Glucoside #9, with argan oil #7 refatting; no sulfate or reset route.
cleansingStrength.counterSignal: Taurate is still the primary anionic and there are four surfactant routes; 'sulfate-free does not automatically mean low'.

conditioningLevel.rationale: High: multiple complementary systems - Hydrolyzed Keratin #6, Argania Spinosa Kernel Oil #7 (payload lipid), starch film-former #8, Amodimethicone #10, cationic Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride #11, Hydrogenated Castor Oil #12 and pearlizing Glycol Distearate #15 (C2 pattern without an early dimethicone).
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: Silicone is mid-list (#10), not early; no humectant cluster.

weightPotential.rationale: High: multiple converging persistent systems (early argan oil #7, amodimethicone #10, cationic guar #11, waxy hydrogenated castor oil #12, glycol distearate #15, keratin #6) in a low-reset mild chassis. Unlike W1 there is no effective sulfate/betaine reset to bound the deposition.
weightPotential.whyThisBand: Several converging deposition routes with weak reset make loss of movement likely.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Moderate would need reset or limited richness to bound residue; the chassis is mild. Amodimethicone's self-limiting deposition is the main reason moderate stays plausible.

focusPrimary.rationale: Repair: name 'Strength & Length + Keratin Oil' and dominant claims 'Anti-Haarbruch Shampoo für strapaziertes Haar', 'verhindert Haarbruch und reduziert Spliss'; verdict repair_supported via a coherent substantive deposition cluster (keratin #6, amodimethicone #10, argan oil #7, film-former #8, guar #11) (F1).

careDirection.limitation: Rinse-off; claims partially quoted from conditioner copy on the retailer page.

focusPrimary.counterSignal: No humectant cluster; positioning evidence is retailer-only and mixes in conditioner text.
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Blind: rich deposition with keratin/amodimethicone/oil -> repair_supported. Unblind: breakage/split-end positioning -> repair.

focusSecondary.rationale: Empty: 'strahlender Glanz' is an outcome of the same deposition route (F2).

usageRole.rationale: Regular: no daily/frequent, reset or treatment trigger (§9 default).

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: No sensitive/itchy/dry-scalp positioning; ordinary fragranced formula.

projection.thicknessRationale: T1 W high: fine not_suited, normal acceptable, coarse ideal. Ordinary target, no T6. T4: W neighbor moderate would raise fine/normal (no flag); coarse stays ideal under W moderate + C high and under C moderate + W high -> no flag. T3 satisfied (coarse ideal).
projection.cleansingIntensityRationale: I1: low -> gentle; differs from the normal bucket's expected regular (I2, kept). I3: neighbor moderate -> regular, which equals the projected bucket's expected intensity where gentle does not -> review_intensity_boundary.
projection.liveComparison: Not evaluated (live rows not in sealed packet).

uncertainties: Positioning is retailer-only and one retailer text mixes conditioner copy ('kräftigende Spülung', 'Pflegespülung repariert'); E1 rules govern projection only, while §7 does not grade claim source tiers for focus. Used the product name plus shampoo-specific retailer claims.

I3 fires on any low/moderate cleansing boundary for an ordinary product because 'gentle' never equals the normal bucket's expected 'regular' - the intensity-boundary review applies even though the flag would move the product toward a green (more recommending) row; standard does not say whether that direction should block.
W1 is anchored on an effective sulfate/betaine base; the standard gives no settled example for the same deposition stack in a mild sulfate-free chassis.
